title: Ephemeral Admin Shortcuts Catalog and Safety Gateway
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight catalog of 'ephemeral admin shortcuts' — parameterized, auditable micro-tasks (runbook snippets) that on-call and support engineers can invoke with scoped, short-lived credentials. The catalog should power a safety gateway that enforces RBAC, dry-run and approval flows, records structured audit events to the telemetry pipeline, and provides an automated rollback path where possible. This ticket scopes the MVP: catalog schema, enforcement layer, invocation API, telemetry contract, and a basic UI in the Ops Console to discover and invoke shortcuts.
background_and_motivation: Support teams repeatedly execute a small set of corrective actions (cache clears, scale-up, restart tasks) that are error-prone when done manually. Existing runbooks are long and contextual; we want fast, safe micro-actions that are discoverable, reversible where feasible, and contain built-in safety checks. This lowers MTTR and reduces blast radius compared to freeform shell access.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical JSON/YAML schema for a shortcut (inputs, preconditions, dry-run script, inverse op metadata, telemetry hooks)
Implement enforcement service (safety gateway) that validates caller RBAC, runs pre-checks, supports dry-run, and returns structured run results
Short-lived credential issuance flow (<=5m TTL) integrated with existing SSO and our operator policy engine
Audit events emitted for every invocation to telemetry (request id, caller, inputs hash, outcome, duration)
Ops Console shows a searchable catalog entry with 'dry-run' / 'run' buttons and a link to the underlying runbook snippet
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after post-mortem for INC-2026-02; initial sketch of catalog schema in Confluence.

2026-03-03: Spike complete comparing two enforcement architectures: operator-sidecar vs centralized safety gateway. Chose centralized safety gateway due to easier policy rollout and unified telemetry. Notes: sidecar has lower latency but higher rollout complexity.

2026-03-05: Catalog schema v0.1 drafted (inputs, preconditions, dry-run script, revert_hint, allowed_roles, cost_estimate). Added required 'inverse_op' field for commands that support automated rollback.
2026-03-08: PoC gateway implemented (internal branch) — validates JWT scopes and returns dry-run diffs. Integrated with mock telemetry sink. Latency tests show median +18ms on synthetic requests.

2026-03-12: Security review sync with SecurOps. Agreed to require two approval flows for shortcuts labeled 'high-impact' and to restrict TTL to 3 minutes for high-impact paths. SecurOps asked for automated replayability constraints on inverse ops.
Next: Harden authentication, add GraphQL catalog query endpoint, wire real telemetry, and ship console discoverability feature flagged to internal beta.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Centralized safety gateway chosen over sidecar due to single place to enforce RBAC and easier telemetry aggregation. Tradeoff: slightly higher tail latency but acceptable for admin operations.
Use JSON schema for catalog for human/editability and validations instead of a custom DSL. Tradeoff: less expressive than a full DSL but faster to onboard PMs/SEs.

Implement 'dry-run' as first-class operation that executes pre-checks and a synthetic planner rather than running the command in a sandbox. Tradeoff: cannot detect environment-only failures but dramatically reduces risk.
Short-lived credential approach (signed JWTs with backend attestation) chosen over impersonation due to auditability and easier revocation. Tradeoff: requires key rotation and careful TTL tuning.

SRE (Marco Diaz) 2026-03-06: Add pre-check that verifies model-serving capacity before scale actions; otherwise automations could throttle user traffic.
Security (Priya Anand) 2026-03-09: High-impact shortcuts must require 2 approvers and encrypted parameter storage. Also requested threat model and replay-resistance tests.
Design (Harper Nguyen) 2026-03-10: Suggest microcopy for danger states in console and clearer rollback affordance.
telemetry_contract: Event schema: ops.shortcut.invocation { request_id, shortcut_id, caller_email, allowed_roles, inputs_hash, dry_run(boolean), outcome, error_codes, duration_ms, gateway_version }. All events must land in grafana/ops-shortcuts and be queryable by shortcut_id and caller.
implementation_notes: Gateway will be a small Go service with a plugin interface for 'executor backends' (k8s-job, helm-rollout, internal-admin-api). Executors run in a restricted namespace and have no direct access to customer keys. Use signed attestation tokens when calling executors. Persist invocation record to audit-store (append-only) before executing.

Implement audit-store persistence and link to identity service (2 days)
Add approval flow and UI affordances for high-impact shortcuts (design review)
Run chaos tests on gateway (simulate executor failures and ensure safe rollback paths)
